title: Merge sort
description:
Merge sort is the classic divide-and-conquer algorithm, and it stays fast on big inputs where selection sort crawls.

1. Write `std::vector<int> merge(const std::vector<int>& left, const std::vector<int>& right)`. Both inputs are already sorted. Build one sorted vector by repeatedly taking the smaller of the two front elements.
2. Write `std::vector<int> mergeSort(const std::vector<int>& values)`. A vector of 0 or 1 elements is already sorted. Otherwise split it in half, sort each half by calling `mergeSort` again, and `merge` the results.

`std::vector<int>(first, last)` makes a new vector from a pair of iterators, which is handy for the two halves.
hints: In `merge`, keep one index into each input. While both have elements left, push the smaller front element and advance that index. Afterwards, one side may still have elements: push them all.
lessonTitle: Sorting, Searching, Big-O and Timing Your Code
